intro: An Oklahoma garage-pop band, loose and melodic.
story: BRONCHO formed in Norman, Oklahoma, in 2010 around Ryan Lindsey, who started out in a band with his two older brothers. Can't Get Past the Lips came out in 2011 and was reissued in 2013, and Just Enough Hip to Be Woman followed in 2014; their song "It's On" closed an episode of HBO's Girls. They played Pickathon in 2015. Lindsey recorded Double Vanity that year, after moving from Norman to Tulsa and driving back to record, and it came out in June 2016 on Dine Alone. Bad Behavior followed on October 12, 2018, and Natural Pleasure on Kung Fu Records in 2025.

intro: Erika Wennerstrom's powerhouse band, back for a third visit.
story: Erika Wennerstrom first played live as Heartless Bastards at the Comet in Northside, Cincinnati, and the band moved to Austin in 2007. Arrow, from February 2012, was their breakthrough, and Restless Ones, their fifth album and second on Partisan, came out on June 16, 2015, the summer of their third Pickathon; NPR said it lets the band stretch out. A Beautiful Life followed on Sweet Unknown Records in 2021.

intro: M.C. Taylor's soul-leaning folk band, back for a second visit.
story: M.C. Taylor and Scott Hirsch began Hiss Golden Messenger in 2007 after the end of their California band The Court & Spark, and moved to North Carolina. Lateness of Dancers, the fifth album and first for Merge, came out on September 9, 2014, with members of Megafaun, Mountain Man and Lambchop; Stereogum made it Album of the Week and The Guardian called it a discreetly charming full-band affair. They played Pickathon in 2014 and 2015. Heart Like a Levee followed in 2016, and Terms of Surrender, from 2019, was nominated for the Grammy for Best Americana Album in 2021. I'm People came out in 2026 on Chrysalis.

Little Freddie King was born Fread Eugene Martin on July 19, 1940, in McComb, Mississippi, and plays a gutbucket Delta style. He made the first electric blues album recorded in New Orleans, with Harmonica Williams in 1969, and has played New Orleans Jazz Fest almost every year since it began. He is a Louisiana Music Hall of Fame inductee, a three-time Blues Performer of the Year in New Orleans and has a Mississippi Blues Trail marker in McComb. He visited Pickathon in 2015, and released Jaw Jackin' Blues in 2020 and Blues Medicine in 2022 on Made Wright Records.
artist_reel_line: He released Jaw Jackin' Blues in 2020 and Blues Medicine in 2022.

intro: A North Carolina duo, here for the second of five visits.
story: Such Jubilee, recorded at Echo Mountain in Asheville, came out on Yep Roc on May 5, 2015, and NPR's Folk Alley said its songs center on the theme of home after two years of constant touring. Andrew Marlin and Emily Frantz played Pickathon that summer, a year after their first visit. They returned in 2017, 2019 and 2023, and as Watchhouse since 2021 released Rituals on Thirty Tigers in 2025.

intro: A Brooklyn songwriter and producer, out of Yellowbirds.
story: Sam Cohen was born on September 28, 1979, in Houston, and founded the psychedelic band Apollo Sunshine in 2001 after he met his bandmates at Berklee. After it ended he formed Yellowbirds, whose Songs from the Vanished Frontier came out on Royal Potato Family on May 28, 2013, and Rolling Stone said he had a clearer idea of what he wanted on it. Yellowbirds broke up in late 2014 as he prepared a solo album, and he played Pickathon in 2015. He has since become a sought-after producer, for Kevin Morby's Singing Saw among others, and released Slow Fawn Music No. 1 on 30th Century Records.

Wand is the Los Angeles group of Cory Hanson, and its debut, Ganglion Reef, came out on Ty Segall's God? imprint at Drag City, with the first three albums arriving within 14 months; Flood said the Segall tie was recommendation enough. They played Pickathon in 2015 and returned in 2018. They have grown from scuzzy volume into intricate, orchestral-tinged rock, and Stereogum made Vertigo, on Drag City in 2024, its Album of the Week.

William Tyler is a Nashville-born guitarist who played with Lambchop for around 13 years and sat in with Silver Jews and Bonnie "Prince" Billy. Impossible Truth, his Merge debut and second solo album, came out on March 19, 2013, produced by Mark Nevers; Tyler called it his '70s singer-songwriter record, just without words. He played Pickathon in 2015 and returned in 2017 with his Modern Country Band, after Modern Country in 2016. Goes West came in 2019, Lost Futures, a duo album with Marisa Anderson, in 2021, and Time Indefinite in 2025.
